hints: Focus on the mechanism type here, nucleophilic addition to the polar C=O bond in ethanal.
Draw what forms when $\text{CN}^-$ attacks the carbonyl carbon, giving $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(O}^-\text{)CN}$ before protonation.
Check that intermediate for four different groups on carbon, location of the charge, and availability of lone pairs to donate.
walkthrough:
**Recall the catalysed mechanism**

This is nucleophilic addition. $\text{NaCN}$ provides the stronger nucleophile $\text{CN}^-$.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CHO} + \text{CN}^- \rightarrow \text{intermediate} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CN}$$

**Draw the intermediate**

$\text{CN}^-$ donates a pair to the $\delta+$ carbonyl carbon, the C=O pi bond breaks and electrons move onto oxygen.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH(O}^-\text{)CN}$$
This is an alkoxide ion. It is later protonated by $\text{HCN}$ to give the cyanohydrin and regenerate $\text{CN}^-$.

**Test statements 1 and 2**

The central carbon is bonded to $\text{CH}_3$, $\text{H}$, $\text{CN}$ and $\text{O}^-$. Four different groups means a chiral centre, so 1 is correct. The oxygen carries a full single negative charge, so 2 is correct.

**Test statement 3**

A nucleophile is an electron pair donor. This anion has full lone pairs on $\text{O}^-$ and is electron rich, so it can act as a nucleophile (in this step it uses the pair to take $\text{H}^+$ as a base). So 3 is also correct.

All of 1, 2 and 3 are correct.

options.A: Correct because statements 1, 2 and 3 are all true. The intermediate $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(O}^-\text{)CN}$ is chiral at carbon, carries one negative charge on oxygen, and with its lone pairs is an electron pair donor, classed as a nucleophile.
options.B: False combination. It correctly includes 1 and 2 but wrongly excludes 3. Students choose this if they think the alkoxide only acts as a base when it takes $\text{H}^+$ and forget that a base is also an electron pair donor and therefore nucleophilic in character.
options.C: False combination. It wrongly excludes 1. Students choose this if they miss the chiral centre, perhaps thinking the negative oxygen makes two groups the same or confusing the planar starting carbonyl with the tetrahedral intermediate.
options.D: False combination. It includes only 1 and misses 2 and 3. Students choose this if they forget the mechanism forms a charged alkoxide $\text{O}^-$ intermediate before protonation.
